cands.name: Ben Harrison

money.note: Covers January 2023 on, primary and general. Party-committee lines are often in-kind staff and mail.
money.source: Alabama Fair Campaign Practices Act system, downloaded Nov 5, 2026

cands.bio: Republican member of the Alabama House of Representatives for District 2 since November 2022. Auburn University engineering graduate. Founded a business and worked as a technical services manager for Kohler.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Ben Harrison was born or raised, or when he moved to Alabama. We found no documented actions or statements from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, land ownership by investors or foreigners, growth and land conservation, immigration or H-1B, police pay, gun laws, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2022 or 2026, and Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for him in 2026. The pages did not show the content of the bills he sponsored. We found no reported controversies and no foreign ties. Details of his business and his years at Kohler are thin.

cands.name: Rick Pressnell

money.note: Covers January 2023 on, primary and general. Party-committee lines are often in-kind staff and mail.
money.source: Alabama Fair Campaign Practices Act system, downloaded Nov 5, 2026

cands.bio: Retired Huntsville police officer, investigator and sergeant (21 years) and retired Army National Guard colonel who also served four years in the U.S. Marine Corps. Since retiring he has maintained and rehabbed rental homes as a sole proprietor. Democratic candidate for Alabama House District 2 in 2026.

endorsements.text: VoteVets (listed on Ballotpedia and named by the candidate in his survey).
Tabitha's List: Candidates You Can Trust, a Sway voting-group voter guide recommendation.

cands.gaps: We found no legislative record, voting history or official filings for Rick Pressnell, because he has not held elected office. He says he wrote Alabama's "Providing False Name to Law Enforcement Officer" law, which Rep. Randy Hinshaw introduced, but we found no record confirming this. His campaign site says data centers and other very large electricity users should cover their own energy costs, but we found no dated statement on banning or approving data centers. We found nothing on his positions on homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, immigration or H-1B, guns, abortion or school choice. His Issues page was cut off mid-sentence, so anything after the maternal and infant mortality section was not read. We found no controversies or foreign ties.

local.label: Roots 100: He says he was born and raised in Limestone County, Alabama, and now lives near the Elk River; the sources are his own campaign site and his Ballotpedia survey answers.

score.why: Raised $3,628, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: He worked 21 years for the Huntsville Police Department as an officer, investigator and sergeant. He retired from the Army National Guard as a colonel after 24+ years of full-time duty, and he runs a sole-proprietor rental and home-rehab business. He has not held elected office.
qual.why: He has management and small-business experience but no legislative service or budget or policy career, which puts him in the middle range for this office.
qual.label: He has management and small-business experience but no legislative service or budget or policy career, which puts him in the middle range for this office.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: In his Ballotpedia survey he said he supports conservation efforts to prevent soil erosion, water depletion, groundwater contamination and biodiversity collapse, and that protecting the Tennessee River and its tributaries from pollution would be a top priority.

back-police-order.evidence: In his Ballotpedia survey he said legislators can provide laws and resources to help law enforcement officers do their jobs better and more safely, and that he favors community policing.
